$comment: Guide A §0 Phase 2 output. One of these lives at <project_root>/guide_c_manifest.json, alongside the prose SOURCE_OF_TRUTH_<project>.md section it's derived from. guide_c_verify.py reads THIS file, not the markdown -- the markdown is for humans/narrative, this is what the orchestrator actually executes. Keeping them in sync is Guide A's job whenever Phase 2 changes.
binary: path to the built binary, relative to project root

roadmap_ids.$comment: Every checkable claim from SOURCE_OF_TRUTH_<project>.md's Phase 1 roadmap, tagged with a short ID (R1, R2, ...) in that markdown. This list must match the IDs actually present in the markdown -- guide_a_coverage_check.py cross-checks both directions: every ID here must exist in the markdown, and every ID in the markdown must appear here or in a 'covers' array below (or be listed as a known gap).
roadmap_ids.R1: one-line restatement of the claim, e.g. 'imports a DXF stock profile'

console_checks.name: string, short id
console_checks.expected_stdout_file: path to an independently-known-correct expected stdout, or null

expected_file_diff.produced: path the binary writes, relative to a temp run dir

gui_checks.name: string, short id
gui_checks.verify_script: verify/verify_render.py, or null to just capture without asserting

project_specific_scripts.name: string, short id, e.g. grbl_dialect_check
project_specific_scripts.note: one line: what this checks and why it doesn't generalize to other projects

known_gaps.reason: why this can't be checked automatically yet -- explicit, not silent

known_limitations: string, e.g. 'T1 M6 tool-change rejected by this grbl build -- pre-existing, not a regression'
